newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BRAZILIAN PENPIX FOR MATCH V ITALY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BRAZILIAN PENPIX FOR MATCH V ITALY.

text.p: Profiles of the Brazilian players likely to face Italy in their Tournoi de France match on Sunday:

Taffarel (Full name Claudio Andre Mergen Taffarel) (Atletico Mineiro) age 30, 76 caps. Back as Brazil's goalkeeper after stepping down following criticism of his performance in 1995 Copa America, vowing not to play again. Had sound game against France although failed to hold ball giving rebound for France's equaliser. Looks set to play third World Cup.

Cafu (Marcos Evangelista de Moraes) (Palmeiras) 26, 46. Has taken over from Jorginho as automatic choice at right back. Good anticipation in defence, very good coming forward, forced France 'keeper Fabien Barthez into fine diving save. Turns 27 on eve of match.

Aldair (Aldair Nascimento Santos) (Roma) 31, 48. Veteran of 1994 World Cup triumph who helped to steady defence against France, coming back into side in place of World Cup centre-back partner Marcio Santos after 4-2 defeat to Norway in Oslo last week.

Celio Silva (Vagno Celio da Nascimento Silva) (Corinthians) 29, 8. Has come on to international stage late in career, looks like developing good partnership with Aldair unless Marcio Santos recovers best form. Possesses one of most powerful shots in game, coming close with 30-metre free kick against French.

Goncalves (Marcelo Goncalves Costa Lopes) (Botafogo) 31, 7. Another late comer to international football after five-year spell in Mexican league. Inspired Botafogo as they won Brazilian championship in 1995. Will start on bench.

Marcio Santos (Marcio Roberto dos Santos) (Atletico Mineiro) 27, 38. Made mark at 1994 World Cup after injuries to three other defenders gave him chance. Troubled spell at Dutch club Ajax led to loss of form. Possible substitute.

Roberto Carlos (Roberto Carlos da Silva) (Real Madrid) 24, 30. Fast and powerful left-back with thunderous shot and wicked swerving free kick with which he scored Brazil's goal against the French. Believes such a goal will help him to cement place in 1998 World Cup side after being controversially left out in 1994.

Dunga (Carlos Caetano Verri) (Jubilo Iwata) 33, 68. Gritty midfielder who captained 1994 World Cup team. Looked set for quiet end to career but surprisingly recalled this year after 18-month absence. His rock-like presence in middle is axis on which Brazil work magic through more gifted players.

Mauro Silva (Mauro da Silva) (Deportivo Coruna) 29, 48. Good distribution combined with solid marking have made him regular in front of defence since 1991 debut. Tireless ball winning work and intelligent running helps Dunga to set up attacking platform. Has yet to score for his country.

Giovanni (Giovanni Silva de Oliveira) (Barcelona) 25, 12. Elegant player who made his name with Santos. Fighting Djalminha and Juninho, who was left out of squad, for main midfield role. Won place from Djalminha in France match after Brazil's defeat in Oslo. Could regain best form with good run in national team.

Leonardo (Leonardo de Araujo) (Paris St Germain) 27, 29. Began career as left back but is now established as an attacking midfielder. Played in 1994 World Cup until he was sent off in second round for uncharacteristically elbowing an opponent and suspended from rest of competition.

Djalminha (Djalma Feitosa Dias) (Palmeiras) 26, 6. Hugely gifted left-footed player who is seen as potential playmaker if he can keep temper under control. Has been sent off three times this year in club matches and was once thrown out of Flamengo for coming to blows with team mate during game. Substitute.

Romario (Romario de Souza Faria) (Flamengo) 31, 44. Brazil's 1994 World Cup hero with five goals, has scored 27 times in his 43 full games. Made comeback this year after two-year absence imposed by coach Mario Zagallo for lack of enthusiasm. Has scored six goals in his last four games.

Ronaldo (Ronaldo Luis Nazario de Lima) (Barcelona) 20, 19. Widely considered best player in world at present. Included in 1994 World Cup squad aged 17, although did not get game. Has scored 12 goals in his 19 appearances. Could mould even better strike partnership with Romario than Bebeto did in 1994.

Paulo Nunes (Arilson de Paulo Nunes) (Gremio) 25, 1. Tricky, talented striker whose call-up was reward after helping his club win South American Libertadores Cup in 1995 and Brazilian championship last year. Substitute for Romario against France.
